changes.after: Use one state value for both a text field and its message.

before: A controlled text input takes its displayed text from a state string through value. Its onChange handler must synchronously request the latest event.target.value. Start with a string, including the empty string, rather than switching between undefined and a string.

The browser supplies the change event; event.target is the input and its value is the current text. setTitle receives that string and requests another render. The status paragraph uses the same state. htmlFor on label matches the input id, so the visible label names the field. Clear sets the same state to an empty string; do not independently edit the DOM value in learner code.

Optional practice: Change the initial title, then verify Clear still empties it. The checks cover these finite behaviors; a matching DOM alone does not prove every implementation choice. The frame supplies React and mounts App. No imports, server, persistence or network are involved.
after: A controlled input gets its text from React state. Its `value` prop shows the state. Its `onChange` handler saves the latest edit back into state.

The browser gives the handler an event. `event.target.value` is the text currently in the input. Pass that text to the setter right away. `htmlFor` matches the input's `id` so the label names the right field.
An empty string, `""`, is a real text value. Use it when the field is blank. Keep this state as a string instead of switching between text and `undefined`.
Make the labeled field and status message follow typing and Clear. Change the state through its setter; do not change the input's displayed text separately.

before.question: The input receives value={title}, but its change handler never calls the setter. What should you expect?
choices: The browser will permanently own the text instead
Edits will not persist as the controlled value
React will automatically copy text into state
before.explanation: A controlled field displays the value React supplies. Its change handler must request the new state; a value prop is not automatic two-way binding.

after.question: What happens if the field has `value={title}` but the change handler never updates title?
choices: The browser takes over the text permanently.
Typed edits do not stay as the controlled value.
React copies the text into state automatically.
after.explanation: The field shows the state React supplies. The handler must update that state to keep the edit.

headings: Keep the field and message together

project.title: Let state control a labeled field
project.task: Connect the labeled text field and status to title state. Make typing update it and Clear empty it.
project.done_when: The field and status agree after typing, deleting text, and clicking Clear.
